To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ROUGE N, the recall-based n-gram overlap measures are the most useful for summarization evaluation, and the ROUGE W, the recall-based word overlap measure, is the least useful.

1) ROUGE is a useful evaluation measure for automatic summarization, 2) ROUGE N, which counts the overlapping n grams, and ROUGE L, which counts the longest overlapping word sequence, are the most useful measures, 3) ROUGE W, which counts the word pairs, is not useful because it is too strict, and 4) ROUGE S is not useful because of the difficulty of its implementation.

ROUGE N is the most effective measure for evaluating the quality of a single summary, ROUGE L and ROUGE W are useful for comparing the quality of multiple summaries, and ROUGE-S is effective for evaluating summaries with varying levels of summarization
